translations.text: After this, when the merciful one had spoken these words to that eagle,
the remaining head also disappeared. Those wings that had moved over to it rose up, and they too stood up to rule, and their claws were thrown into turmoil.
Then they too disappeared, and all their flesh was scorched. The earth trembled greatly, and I too trembled with overwhelming agitation and awoke in great fear.
I said to my soul, “You have brought all this upon me while searching out the ways of the Most High.”
My soul grew weak, and my spirit became very sick. I had no strength at all because of the great fear that terrified me that night.
And now I pray to the Most High to strengthen me continually.
I said, “Lord, my Lord, if I have found favor in your eyes, and if I have made many vows to you, and if my prayer has risen before your face,
save me and strengthen me, and tell your servant the meaning of this terrifying dream, so that my soul may rejoice fully.
For you have made me blessed by showing me the last days and the end of the ages of the world.”
He said to me, “This is the meaning of that dream you saw:
The eagle rising from the sea is the fourth kingdom, which appeared in a dream to your brother Daniel.
But I did not explain it to him as I now explain it to you.
Look, the days are coming when a kingdom will arise on the earth, more terrifying than all the kingdoms that came before it.
Twelve kings will reign in it.
The one who reigns second will be strong, and his days will be longer than those of the twelve.
This is the meaning of those twelve wings of its that you saw.
As for what you saw speaking a word that came not from its head but from the middle of its body,
This is what it means: great turmoil will arise from within the body of that kingdom, and it will be shaken toward collapse. Yet it will not fall at that time, but will remain in power.
and what you saw—heads coming out of its wings—
this is its meaning: eight kings will arise in it. Their reigns will be evil and their days short, and two of them will quickly perish in the middle of their lives.
But four kingdoms will be kept until their time comes for its end, and two will be kept for [?].
As for what you saw—its three heads remaining silent—
this is its meaning: in the last days the Most High will raise up three kings. They will renew many things in it and torment the earth
and those who live in it with great terror, more than all those who came before them. For this reason they were called the heads of the eagle.
For those heads of the kingdom are its end.
As for what you saw—its one larger head disappearing—one of them alone will die in his bed, but in torment.
The two who remain will die in war.
And one [?] afterward, he too will die in war.
As for what I saw—the two heads that moved into the head on the right—
this is its meaning: these are the ones whom the Most High has kept for the end. Through them the beginning of destruction will come, and there will be great turmoil, as you saw.
As for this lion that you saw rising from the wilderness, roaring and speaking to that eagle and reproaching it for its sins—all these words that you heard—

This is the one whom the Most High has kept for the last days, from the descendants of David. He will come forth and tell them their sins, rebuke them for their wrongdoing, and plainly set their punishment before them.
First he will bring them before the judgment while they are still alive. Then, after rebuking them, he will destroy them.
And he will mercifully redeem the remaining people, those who have survived within my borders, and make them rejoice until the day of judgment arrives, of which I told you before.
Such is the dream you saw, and such is its interpretation.
The Most High has enabled you alone to know this mystery.
But write everything you saw in a book and put it in a hidden place.
Teach it to the wise among the people whom you know to be able to keep this mystery in their hearts.
As for you, remain here another seven days, so that you may see what the Most High wishes to show you.
Then he went away from me. When all the people heard that those seven days had passed and I had not entered the city, they all gathered, young and old, and came to me and said:
How have we sinned against you, and how have we wronged you, that you should leave us and stay in this place?
For you alone remain to us out of all the prophets, like a single cluster of grapes out of all that is gathered, like a lamp in a dark place, and like a harbor for a ship amid a storm.
“Oh, has the calamity that has overtaken us not been enough for us?
If you too have abandoned me, it would have been better for us to have remained in the burning of Zion.
For we are no better than those who died there.” And they wept loudly.
I answered them and said, “Have faith and do not grieve, house of Jacob.
For we are remembered before the Most High, and the Mighty One has not forgotten us.
I will not abandon you or go far away from you. But I came to this place to ask about the destruction of Zion and to seek mercy for the suffering of our joy.
Now all of you go into your homes, and I myself will come to you after those days.”
The people went into their homes, as I had told them.
I remained in that place in the wilderness for seven days, as he had commanded me. During those days I lived only on the fruit of the wilderness and ate wild plants.
Then, after seven days, I dreamed a dream at night.
I saw a great wind rising from the sea, and all its waves were stirred up.
I saw that wind come out of the sea in the likeness of a man. Then that man flew with the clouds of heaven, and wherever he turned his face and looked, everything before him immediately trembled.
Wherever his voice reached, all who heard it melted, as wild honey melts when brought near a fire.
Then I saw countless people gathering from the four winds of heaven to fight the man who had come out of the sea.
Then he built a great mountain for himself and flew onto it.
I tried to discover where that mountain had been built, but I could not.
Then all those who had gathered against him to fight him were greatly afraid of him, but they nevertheless plotted to fight him.
Then, when they rushed at him and came against him, he did not raise his hands or lift a spear or any weapon of war.

Instead, however, he sent streams of fire from his mouth, a flame of fire from his lips, and fiery coals from his tongue like a whirlwind. All those streams of fire, that flame of fire, and those fiery coals joined together and became like a whirlwind.

It descended upon the great multitude who had rushed at him to kill him and burned them all, until nothing remained of them except the dust of their ashes and the smoke of their burning. Then I woke up.
And after this I saw that man come down from that mountain and call to himself many others who hated him.

Many people came to him. Some of them were joyful, some were sorrowful, and some were bound in chains. Then, as their number increased, I became frightened and woke up. I prayed to the Most High and said:
“Previously you showed your servant this glory of yours and assured me that you would hear my prayer.
Now tell me also the interpretation of this dream.
But as I consider it, woe to those who are alive in those days, and even more to those who are not!
For they grieve without knowing what is reserved for them in the last days, which have not yet come upon them.
As for those who are alive, they have known its end.
And for this reason, woe to them, because they will see great distress and much suffering, as I saw in this dream.
Yet it is better to suffer and reach this time than to pass out of the world like a cloud without knowing what will happen afterward.”
He answered me and said, “I will tell you the interpretation of this dream of yours, and I will also explain to you what you said to me.
Since you spoke about those who remain and are alive, this is the explanation:
They are the ones who will see that suffering in those days. He himself will preserve those who undergo that suffering, those who have good deeds and faith in the Most High and Mighty One.
But know that the living are more blessed than the dead.
The interpretation of your dream is this: the man whom you saw coming out of the midst of the sea—
this is the one whom the Most High has kept for many days so that the world might be redeemed through him. He will bring order to those who remain.
As for what you saw coming from his mouth—fire, flame, and coals like a whirlwind—
and how he did not raise a spear or a weapon of war, yet killed the great multitude who rushed at him and came to kill him, this is the explanation:
Days are coming when the Most High is to redeem those who dwell on the earth.
At that time they will devise plans.
They will fight among themselves, city against city, region against region, people against people, and kingdom against kingdom.
And when this happens and the signs that I showed you earlier come to pass, the man whom you saw coming out of the sea—
when all the peoples hear his voice, they will abandon, each in their own regions, the wars they wage against one another.
They will gather together in countless numbers, as you saw, intending to come and kill him.
But he will stand on the summit of Mount Zion.
Zion will come and appear, prepared in every way and fortified, just as you saw the mountain emerge by itself and come into being without human hands.
He is the Son who will rebuke the nations for their sins, those who became like a storm. He will set before them the wickedness of their deeds and the judgment by which they will be severely judged.
They became like a blazing fire, and he will destroy them together with their sins, without effort—those who became like burning coals.
And as for what you saw, that many gathered to him [?].

These are the nine nations who were taken captive from their land in the days of Shalmaneser, king of Persia. He took them captive during his reign and settled them beyond the river, and they turned away and became different.
They themselves devised this plan: to leave the tribes of their people and go into a land where no human being had ever lived,
so that they might keep their law, which they had not kept in their own land.
They entered through the narrow entrance of the Euphrates.
At that time the Most High performed a miracle for them and stopped the sources of the river so that they could cross.
The land was a journey of a year and a half away, and the name of the land was Azaph.
They remained there until the last days. Then, when they are to return,
the Most High will again stop the sources of the river so that they can cross.
This is why you saw the multitude of the people whom they took away and who were found within my blessed borders.
When he has destroyed those many peoples who gathered against him, he will then strengthen the people who remain.
At that time he will show them his miracles.
And I said to him, “Lord, my lord, tell me this also: why did I see a man coming up from the midst of the sea?”
He said to me, “Just as no one can know what is in the depths of the sea, so no one living on earth can know the Son or those who are with him, except when his time and his day have arrived.
And this is the interpretation of the dream you saw, and for this reason I showed it to you alone.
For your sorrow has departed, and you have followed my [?] and sought my law.
You have devoted your life to understanding and made wisdom your mother.
For this reason I have shown you these things, because your reward is with the Most High. Come, then, after a few days, for I have something else to tell you, and I will explain a wonder to you.”
I went away and passed through the wilderness, praising and thanking God for the glorious things he does in every age,
and for how he orders the years and what happens in each year. I remained there three days.
And on the third day, while I was sitting under a tree.
A voice came from opposite that tree and said, “Ezra, Ezra!” I said, “Here I am,” and I rose and stood.
He said to me, “I revealed myself to Moses and spoke to him at the thornbush when my people were enslaved in Egypt.
I sent him, brought my people out of Egypt, and led them to Mount Sinai. I kept him with me for many days.
I told him many wonders, revealed to him the mysteries of the times, and made known to him the end of the age.
I commanded him and said to him, “Make this matter known, but keep this matter hidden.”
And now I say to you:
Keep in your heart the signs I told you about, the dream you saw, and the interpretation you heard.
For you will be taken away from humankind, and you will live with my Son, where those like you are, until the world comes to an end.
For the world has passed its youth, and its days have grown old.
For the world was divided into ten parts, and it has reached the tenth.
Half of the tenth remains.
Now, then, put your house in order, comfort those among your people who are sorrowful, instruct those among them who are wise, and free yourself from mortal life.
Leave behind mortal thoughts, cast off the burden of human life, and put on what does not die. Leave behind sorrowful thoughts, and hurry to depart from this world.
For the evil you have now seen has arrived, and something worse than it will come again.
For as the world grows old and weak, the wickedness of those who live in it increases.
For righteousness disappears and falsehood arises, because this eagle you saw hastens toward its end.
I answered him and said, “Then I will speak before you.
For I am going away, Lord, and as you commanded me, I will teach the people who are alive now. Who, then, will teach those who are born afterward?
For the world lies in darkness, and those who live in it have no light.
For your law has been burned, and no one knows what you have done or what you are going to do.

If I have found favor before you, send the Holy Spirit upon me, and I will write everything that has happened in the world from its beginning, and everything that was written in your law, so that people who wish to live may find the way of life.”
He answered me and said, “Go, gather your people, and tell them not to look for you for forty days.
Prepare many tablets for yourself, and take with you Seraiah, Dabria, Shelemiah, Elkanah, and Asahel, these five men, for they are skilled in writing.
Come here, and I will light a lamp of wisdom in your heart. It will not go out until you finish everything you are to write.
When you have finished, make some things public, but hide others and give them to the wise. Tomorrow at this hour you will begin to write.”
And I went as he commanded me and gathered all the people.
I said to them, “Israel, listen to these words.
Long ago your ancestors lived in the land of Egypt, and he redeemed them from there.
They received the law of life but did not keep it, and you who came after them also rejected it.
He gave us a land and gave us the land of Zion as our inheritance. But both you and your ancestors sinned and did not keep the ways of the Most High that he commanded you.
For he who gave you your law at the proper time is a righteous judge.
Now you are here, but your brothers are farther inland than you.
And if you discipline your hearts, correct your thoughts, and guard your lives, you will not die.
For judgment comes after death, and it will not bring us to life. At that time the names of the righteous will be revealed, and the deeds of sinners will be uncovered.
Let none of you come to me, and do not seek me for forty days.
I took those five men, as he had commanded me, and we went into the wilderness and stayed there.
On the following day a voice came and called me. It said to me, “Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I give you to drink.”
I opened my mouth, and he gave me a cup full of water, whose color resembled fire.
I took it and drank, and my heart poured forth abundant wisdom. Understanding grew weighty within my shoulders, and my spirit was kept alert and remembered.
My mouth was opened and did not close again.
And the Most High gave wisdom to those five men, and they wrote all this in characters they did not know, in sequence. They stayed there for forty days, and they wrote during the day.
And in the evening they ate food, while I spoke during the day and did not remain silent at night.
During those forty days, ninety-four books were written.
Then, when those forty days were completed, the Most High spoke to me and said, “Make public what you wrote first, and let everyone read it, both those who are worthy and those who are unworthy.
But keep this so that you may give it to the wise among the people.
For in them are a lamp of light, a spring of wisdom, and knowledge like a flowing stream.”

And I did so in the fourth year of the sabbaths of years, after the year of judgment, in the year five thousand, on the tenth of darkness [?], in the third month; his days were ninety-two. At that time they took Ezra and brought him to the land of those like him, after he had written all this. And he was called the scribe of the wisdom of the Most High forever and ever.
